images.caption: Figure 1:Self-HPOrecursively improves the harness and policy using the agent itself.Left:In each H-step, the current policy proposes an improved harness, and each P-step then updates the policy through reinforcement learning with the optimized harness.Right:Average resolve rate over SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Multilingual, and SWE-Bench Pro along the H- and P-steps. Policy-only and Harness-only denote the RLVR(Peng et al., 2026)and Self-Harness(Zhang et al., 2026a)baselines.

Figure 2:Overview of Self-HPO.Top (H-step):The frozen policy analyzes the agent’s failures on the search set and proposes new harness candidates.Bottom (P-step):With the updated harness, the policy evolves through reinforcement learning.
The updated policy becomes the next harness proposer, while tasks never resolved during this P-step form the next search set.

Figure 3:Optimization trajectories across harness and policy updates.Resolve rates (%) on SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Multilingual, and SWE-Bench Pro are shown on the common Base–H1H_{1}–P1P_{1}–H2H_{2}–P2P_{2}schedule.
Self-HPO alternates H- and P-steps, whereas Self-Harness and RLVR update only the harness and policy, respectively.
Markers with dashed outlines indicate steps at which the corresponding method performs no update.

Figure 6:Best-so-far performance during harness evolution on SWE-Bench Verified.Circles show individual candidate scores.
Candidates 1–6 are shared, while 7–12 belong to the separate Self-Harness and Self-HPO branches.
Vertical increases and stars mark Self-HPO’s two P-steps.
Dashed horizontal lines show Base and final RLVR performance.
